headline: South Korea central bank raises interest rates to 3.25%
summary: The Bank of Korea increased its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to 3.25%, citing persistent inflation, economic growth, and financial stability risks.
why: Central bank rate decisions are primary drivers of currency value and domestic borrowing costs.

impacts.name: South Korean Won
impacts.why: Higher interest rates typically attract foreign capital, strengthening the local currency.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Monetary tightening is a direct response to inflation, usually leading to higher yields and currency appreciation.
